categories.title: Basics
categories.description: Small questions used to demonstrate Quizbank.

questions.stem: In most programming languages, what is the common term for a value like `true` or `false`?

choices.rationale: The data type with two truth values is typically called a Boolean.

feedback.correct: Yep. Boolean is the two-valued logical type.
feedback.incorrect: The two-valued logical type is called a Boolean.

questions.solution: The correct answer is **Boolean**. It represents a truth value, usually `true` or `false`.
questions.author: Tim Rossiter

questions.stem: Which of the following are **comparison-based** sorting algorithms? Select all that apply.

choices.rationale: Uses counts of keys; not comparison-based.
Distributes by digit or bucket; not comparison-based.

feedback.correct: Merge and Quick are the comparison-based ones here.
feedback.incorrect: Counting and radix sort avoid direct key comparisons.

questions.solution: **Merge sort** and **Quick sort** are comparison sorts; **Counting** and **Radix** are not.
questions.author: Tim Rossiter

questions.stem: In a binary search tree, an **in-order traversal** visits the keys in nondecreasing order.

feedback.correct: Correct. That is the useful property of in-order traversal on a BST.
feedback.incorrect: In-order traversal yields a sorted sequence for a valid BST.

questions.solution: BST ordering plus left-node-right traversal produces sorted keys.
questions.author: Tim Rossiter

questions.stem: A circuit has a current of 3 A through a 2 Ω resistor. What is the voltage across the resistor?

feedback.correct: Correct. Ohm's law gives $V = IR = 3 \times 2 = 6$ V.

questions.author: Tim Rossiter

questions.stem: Name the data structure that uses the **LIFO** discipline.

feedback.correct: LIFO is the defining behavior of a stack.

questions.solution: A **stack** is LIFO: the most recently pushed item is popped first.
questions.author: Tim Rossiter

questions.stem: A loop that never reaches its termination condition is commonly called an {{blank}} loop.
questions.author: Tim Rossiter

answers: The loop accesses `values[4]`, which is outside the array.
